label: copy-phase input token 0 (fed-back output 0), from recall_idx 2 on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the input (the model own previous output fed back) is the digit 0, i.e. orig(recall_idx-1) == 0. It is essentially perfectly precise for recall_idx >= 2 (rate 1.0 on dev). When 0 is the first original token and is fed back at recall_idx 1 (the step right after the first output), it fires only very weakly (~0.02-0.06 of max) - these account for the ~3% missed steps but only ~0.1% of the mass. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, even on input 0, and never on any other token. Magnitude is high and fairly uniform (median ~0.82 of max); in examples the strongest activations (~0.98-1.0) come at 0 inputs late in the copy, close to the end of the sequence, and earlier 0s sit at ~0.7-0.88.

issues: Minor: at recall_idx 1, about 14% of the 0 inputs get weak activations (0.02-0.08 of max). On the test split these are 2333 steps holding 0.1% of the activation mass. Adding recall_idx 1 to the predicate raises recall to 1.0 but drops precision to 0.84 (F1 0.914), so leaving it out is the better choice. The explanation already describes this case honestly.
No false positives on the test split (precision 1.000, F1 0.985, mass recall 0.999). I reproduced all of these numbers.
Phase claims check out. The feature has 0 activations in the original and delimiter phases, and only 10 of 76,981 dev activations are on other tokens (s 5, r 4, p 1).
The claim that magnitude rises late in the copy was not tested and is stated as anecdotal. The by-t / to_go mass profile roughly fits it, but it is not part of the label.
